objects.description: A non-owning string view class for referencing a sized sequence of characters without copying. Similar to std::string_view; provides iteration, substring, find/rfind, prefix/suffix removal, and comparison utilities. It holds a pointer and length; caller must ensure the referenced memory remains valid.

Main C++ regular expression class of RE2. Represents a compiled regex that is safe for concurrent use. Provides matching (full/partial/consume), replacement, extraction, quoting, and program statistics. Constructed from a pattern string/StringPiece with optional Options.
Configuration class for RE2 construction and behavior. Controls encoding, syntax, matching semantics, logging, memory budget, and related toggles. Provides ParseFlags for internal compilation flags.

Helper class representing a destination for a captured submatch with an associated parser. Created implicitly from pointers passed to RE2 matching APIs; wraps typed pointers and knows how to parse strings into them.
Thread-safe lazy initializer wrapper for a process-lifetime RE2 instance, intended for global/static usage. Allocates the RE2 on first use and never deletes it.

A set of regexes compiled together for simultaneous matching. Supports adding patterns, compiling once, and then matching text to obtain indices of matching regexes; also reports certain DFA-related errors.
Hook payload struct describing a DFA state cache reset event: includes the configured state budget and the cache size at reset time.
Hook payload struct for DFA search failure events. Currently empty and serves as a signal type.

objects.definition:
#define DECLARE_HOOK(type)                  \
  using type##Callback = void(const type&); \
  void Set##type##Hook(type##Callback* cb); \
  type##Callback* Get##type##Hook();

DECLARE_HOOK(DFAStateCacheReset)
objects.description: Type alias for the callback signature for DFAStateCacheReset hooks: pointer to function taking const DFAStateCacheReset& and returning void. Also declares setter/getter functions for the hook. Note: only the alias is a type; functions are declared elsewhere.
Type alias for the callback signature for DFASearchFailure hooks: pointer to function taking const DFASearchFailure& and returning void. Setter/getter functions are declared by the macro.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::begin
functions.description: Returns a const iterator to the first character of the piece. Use for range iteration.
requirements: The StringPiece must refer to a valid memory range for iteration; if size()==0, begin()==end().

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::end
functions.description: Returns a const iterator one past the last character of the piece.
requirements: Safe to use when size()==0; end()==begin().

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::rbegin
functions.description: Returns a const reverse iterator to the last character of the piece.
requirements: If size()==0, rbegin()==rend().

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::rend
functions.description: Returns a const reverse iterator one before the first character (reverse end).
requirements: If size()==0, rbegin()==rend().

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::size
functions.description: Returns the number of characters in the piece.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::length
functions.description: Returns the number of characters in the piece (alias of size()).

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::empty
functions.description: Returns true if the piece has zero length.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::operator[]
functions.description: Returns the character at index i without bounds checking.
requirements: i must be less than size(); otherwise behavior is undefined.
The underlying data_ pointer must point to at least i+1 accessible characters.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first character (may be NULL if size()==0 and data_ is NULL).
requirements: Do not dereference the returned pointer if size()==0 and data()==NULL.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::remove_prefix
functions.description: Advances the start of the piece by n characters, shrinking its size.
requirements: n must be less than or equal to size(); otherwise behavior is undefined.
Resulting piece must still refer to valid memory.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::remove_suffix
functions.description: Shrinks the piece by removing n characters from the end.
requirements: n must be less than or equal to size(); otherwise behavior is undefined.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::set
functions.description: Resets the piece to point to a C string str; size becomes strlen(str). If str is NULL, size becomes 0.
requirements: str may be NULL; when NULL, data_ becomes NULL and size_ becomes 0.
When non-NULL, str must be NUL-terminated.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::as_string
functions.description: Returns a std::string with a copy of the piece’s contents.
requirements: If data()==NULL and size()>0, behavior is unspecified; in normal usage, data() should be non-NULL when size()>0.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::ToString
functions.description: Returns a std::string copy of the piece (alias of as_string()).
requirements: If data()==NULL and size()>0, behavior is unspecified; typically data() should be valid when size()>0.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::CopyToString
functions.description: Assigns the piece’s contents to *target, replacing its previous contents.
requirements: target must be non-NULL.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::AppendToString
functions.description: Appends the piece’s contents to *target.
requirements: target must be non-NULL.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::copy
functions.signature: re2::StringPiece::size_type copy(char* buf, re2::StringPiece::size_type n, re2::StringPiece::size_type pos = 0) const
functions.description: Copies up to n characters starting at position pos into buf. Returns the number of characters copied.
requirements: buf must be non-NULL if n>0.
pos must be less than or equal to size(); copying from past-the-end copies 0.
Copies min(n, size()-pos) bytes; buf must have sufficient space.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::substr
functions.signature: re2::StringPiece substr(re2::StringPiece::size_type pos = 0, re2::StringPiece::size_type n = re2::StringPiece::npos) const
functions.description: Returns a StringPiece referencing a subrange starting at pos with length up to n (clamped to size()).
requirements: pos must be less than or equal to size(); if pos==size(), result is empty.
Result references the same underlying memory; it does not copy.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::compare
functions.description: Lexicographically compares this piece to x using memcmp semantics. Returns -1, 0, or 1.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::starts_with
functions.description: Returns true if this piece starts with x (or if x is empty).

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::ends_with
functions.description: Returns true if this piece ends with x (or if x is empty).

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::contains
functions.description: Returns true if s occurs as a substring of this piece.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::find
functions.signature: re2::StringPiece::size_type find(const re2::StringPiece& s, re2::StringPiece::size_type pos = 0) const
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of substring s at or after pos. Returns index or npos.
requirements: pos may be from 0 to size(); values > size() result in npos.

functions.name: re2::StringPiece::rfind
functions.signature: re2::StringPiece::size_type rfind(const re2::StringPiece& s, re2::StringPiece::size_type pos = re2::StringPiece::npos) const
functions.description: Finds the last occurrence of substring s at or before pos. Returns index or npos.
requirements: pos is the position to start reverse search; typical semantics apply (npos means end).

functions.name: re2::operator==
functions.signature: bool operator==(const re2::StringPiece& x, const re2::StringPiece& y)
functions.description: Returns true if x and y have equal length and identical bytes.

functions.name: re2::operator!=
functions.signature: bool operator!=(const re2::StringPiece& x, const re2::StringPiece& y)
functions.description: Returns true if x and y are not equal.

functions.name: re2::operator<
functions.signature: bool operator<(const re2::StringPiece& x, const re2::StringPiece& y)
functions.description: Lexicographical comparison of two StringPiece values.

functions.name: re2::operator>
functions.signature: bool operator>(const re2::StringPiece& x, const re2::StringPiece& y)
functions.description: Returns y < x.

functions.name: re2::operator<=
functions.signature: bool operator<=(const re2::StringPiece& x, const re2::StringPiece& y)
functions.description: Returns !(x > y).

functions.name: re2::operator>=
functions.signature: bool operator>=(const re2::StringPiece& x, const re2::StringPiece& y)
functions.description: Returns !(x < y).

functions.name: re2::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& o, const re2::StringPiece& p)
functions.description: Inserts the contents of p into output stream o.
requirements: o must be a valid std::ostream reference.
p may be empty; if p.data()==NULL and p.size()==0, nothing is written.

functions.name: re2::RE2::ok
functions.description: Returns true iff the RE2 object was constructed successfully (error_code()==NoError).

functions.name: re2::RE2::pattern
functions.description: Returns the original pattern string used to construct this RE2.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the RE2 object.

functions.name: re2::RE2::error
functions.description: If construction failed, returns a descriptive error message; otherwise, returns an empty string.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the RE2 object.

functions.name: re2::RE2::error_code
functions.description: Returns the error code from construction; NoError if successful.

functions.name: re2::RE2::error_arg
functions.description: Returns the portion of the pattern that caused a construction error (empty if none).
requirements: Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the RE2 object.

functions.name: re2::RE2::ProgramSize
functions.description: Returns an approximate measure of the forward program size (cost). Larger means more expensive.

functions.name: re2::RE2::ReverseProgramSize
functions.description: Returns an approximate measure of the reverse program size.

functions.name: re2::RE2::ProgramFanout
functions.description: Optionally fills histogram with program fanout bucketed by powers of 2 and returns index of largest non-empty bucket.
requirements: histogram may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be populated/modified.

functions.name: re2::RE2::ReverseProgramFanout
functions.description: Like ProgramFanout, but for the reverse program.
requirements: histogram may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be populated/modified.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Regexp
functions.description: Returns the underlying parsed Regexp object for advanced use. Not for general use.
requirements: Pointer is valid while the RE2 object exists; caller must not delete it.

functions.name: re2::RE2::FullMatchN
functions.signature: static bool FullMatchN(const re2::StringPiece& text, const re2::RE2& re, const re2::RE2::Arg* const args[], int n)
functions.description: Array-based matching: checks whether text matches re fully and assigns captured submatches to args[0..n-1].
requirements: args may be NULL if n==0; otherwise must point to an array of at least n pointers to Arg.
Each Arg must be initialized with a pointer of an appropriate type or nullptr to ignore.
On failure, pointees are not modified.
n must be >= 0.

functions.name: re2::RE2::PartialMatchN
functions.signature: static bool PartialMatchN(const re2::StringPiece& text, const re2::RE2& re, const re2::RE2::Arg* const args[], int n)
functions.description: Array-based matching: checks whether some substring of text matches re and assigns captures.
requirements: args/n as for FullMatchN.
On failure, pointees are not modified.
n must be >= 0.

functions.name: re2::RE2::ConsumeN
functions.signature: static bool ConsumeN(re2::StringPiece* input, const re2::RE2& re, const re2::RE2::Arg* const args[], int n)
functions.description: Array-based anchored matching at the start of *input. On success, advances *input past the match (only if the match is non-empty) and assigns captures.
requirements: input must be non-NULL; it is modified iff the function returns true and the match is non-empty.
args/n as for FullMatchN.
n must be >= 0.

functions.name: re2::RE2::FindAndConsumeN
functions.signature: static bool FindAndConsumeN(re2::StringPiece* input, const re2::RE2& re, const re2::RE2::Arg* const args[], int n)
functions.description: Array-based unanchored search within *input. On success, advances *input past the match and assigns captures.
requirements: input must be non-NULL and is modified iff the function returns true and the match is non-empty.
args/n as for FullMatchN.
n must be >= 0.

functions.name: re2::RE2::FullMatch
functions.signature: template <typename... A> static bool FullMatch(const re2::StringPiece& text, const re2::RE2& re, A&&... a)
functions.description: Convenience variadic wrapper for FullMatchN. Matches entire text against re and assigns captures to arguments.
requirements: Arguments a... must be pointers of acceptable types (e.g., std::string*, StringPiece*, numeric pointers), or nullptr to ignore.
On failure, pointees are not modified.

functions.name: re2::RE2::PartialMatch
functions.signature: template <typename... A> static bool PartialMatch(const re2::StringPiece& text, const re2::RE2& re, A&&... a)
functions.description: Convenience variadic wrapper for PartialMatchN. Matches a substring of text against re and assigns captures.
requirements: Arguments a... must be pointers of acceptable types or nullptr to ignore.
On failure, pointees are not modified.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Consume
functions.signature: template <typename... A> static bool Consume(re2::StringPiece* input, const re2::RE2& re, A&&... a)
functions.description: Convenience variadic wrapper for ConsumeN. Anchored at the start of *input; advances *input on success.
requirements: input must be non-NULL and may be modified.
Arguments a... must be pointers of acceptable types or nullptr to ignore.

functions.name: re2::RE2::FindAndConsume
functions.signature: template <typename... A> static bool FindAndConsume(re2::StringPiece* input, const re2::RE2& re, A&&... a)
functions.description: Convenience variadic wrapper for FindAndConsumeN. Searches within *input; advances *input on success.
requirements: input must be non-NULL and may be modified.
Arguments a... must be pointers of acceptable types or nullptr to ignore.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Replace
functions.signature: static bool Replace(std::string* str, const re2::RE2& re, const re2::StringPiece& rewrite)
functions.description: Replaces the first match of re in *str with rewrite, supporting backslash-escaped group indices (\0..\9). Returns true if a replacement occurred.
requirements: str must be non-NULL and is modified on success.
rewrite may reference capture groups by \N; groups beyond those present are invalid.
If re does not match, *str is unchanged.

functions.name: re2::RE2::GlobalReplace
functions.signature: static int GlobalReplace(std::string* str, const re2::RE2& re, const re2::StringPiece& rewrite)
functions.description: Replaces successive non-overlapping matches of re in *str with rewrite. Returns the number of replacements made.
requirements: str must be non-NULL and is modified.
Replacements are not subject to re-matching; overlapping matches are not replaced.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Extract
functions.signature: static bool Extract(const re2::StringPiece& text, const re2::RE2& re, const re2::StringPiece& rewrite, std::string* out)
functions.description: If re matches text, writes the rewritten string (with substitutions) to *out and returns true; otherwise leaves *out unaffected and returns false.
requirements: out must be non-NULL.
REQUIRES: text must not alias any part of *out.
rewrite must be well-formed with respect to re’s capture groups.

functions.name: re2::RE2::QuoteMeta
functions.description: Returns a version of unquoted with all regexp meta-characters escaped so it matches the literal input.

functions.name: re2::RE2::PossibleMatchRange
functions.signature: bool PossibleMatchRange(std::string* min, std::string* max, int maxlen) const
functions.description: Computes lexicographic min/max strings of length up to maxlen such that any anchored match s satisfies min <= s <= max. Returns true on success.
requirements: min and max must be non-NULL.
maxlen must be non-negative.

functions.name: re2::RE2::NumberOfCapturingGroups
functions.description: Returns the number of capturing groups in the regexp (excluding the overall match), or -1 if the regexp is invalid.

functions.name: re2::RE2::NamedCapturingGroups
functions.description: Returns a map from capture group names to their leftmost indices. Valid until the RE2 is destroyed.
requirements: Returned reference is invalidated when the RE2 object is destroyed.

functions.name: re2::RE2::CapturingGroupNames
functions.description: Returns a map from capture group indices to their names for named groups. Valid until the RE2 is destroyed.
requirements: Returned reference is invalidated when the RE2 object is destroyed.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Match
functions.signature: bool Match(const re2::StringPiece& text, size_t startpos, size_t endpos, re2::RE2::Anchor re_anchor, re2::StringPiece* submatch, int nsubmatch) const
functions.description: General matching: searches text[startpos:endpos] with the given anchoring. On success, fills submatch[0..nsubmatch-1] with match and captures.
requirements: startpos and endpos define a valid range within text (0 <= startpos <= endpos <= text.size()).
submatch may be NULL if nsubmatch==0; otherwise must point to an array of at least nsubmatch elements.
Caveat: submatch[] may be clobbered even on match failure.
Passing text == StringPiece(NULL,0) is allowed but submatch[i].data() will be NULL for unmatched or empty matches.

functions.name: re2::RE2::CheckRewriteString
functions.signature: bool CheckRewriteString(const re2::StringPiece& rewrite, std::string* error) const
functions.description: Validates that rewrite is well-formed for this regexp (sufficient capture groups; valid escapes). Returns true if valid.
requirements: error may be NULL; if non-NULL and the check fails, *error is populated with a message.

functions.name: re2::RE2::MaxSubmatch
functions.description: Returns the maximum capture group index referenced by rewrite (e.g., returns 2 for "foo \\2,\\1").

functions.name: re2::RE2::Rewrite
functions.signature: bool Rewrite(std::string* out, const re2::StringPiece& rewrite, const re2::StringPiece* vec, int veclen) const
functions.description: Appends to *out the rewrite string with backreference substitutions using the captures in vec[0..veclen-1]. Returns true on success.
requirements: out must be non-NULL.
rewrite must be well-formed; CheckRewriteString() can be used to ensure success.
vec must point to an array of at least veclen StringPiece entries representing captures including $0 if required.

functions.name: re2::RE2::options
functions.description: Returns the options used to construct this RE2 object.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the RE2 object.

functions.name: re2::RE2::CRadix
functions.signature: template <typename T> static re2::RE2::Arg CRadix(T* ptr)
functions.description: Wraps a numeric pointer to parse in C-style radix (0x=hex, 0=octal, otherwise decimal) when used as a capture argument.
requirements: ptr must be non-NULL if you expect a value to be stored; passing NULL would result in the parser receiving a null destination which is not documented to be safe.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Hex
functions.signature: template <typename T> static re2::RE2::Arg Hex(T* ptr)
functions.description: Wraps a numeric pointer to parse as base-16 when used as a capture argument.
requirements: ptr must be non-NULL if you expect a value to be stored.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Octal
functions.signature: template <typename T> static re2::RE2::Arg Octal(T* ptr)
functions.description: Wraps a numeric pointer to parse as base-8 when used as a capture argument.
requirements: ptr must be non-NULL if you expect a value to be stored.

functions.name: re2::LazyRE2::operator*
functions.description: Returns a reference to the lazily-initialized RE2. Use like a pointer dereference.
requirements: The LazyRE2 must have been initialized via braced initialization of pattern_/options_. Initialization occurs on first use and the RE2 object is leaked intentionally (never deleted).
Thread-safe via std::call_once.

functions.name: re2::LazyRE2::operator->
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the lazily-initialized RE2. Use to access RE2 members.
requirements: Same as operator*(): initialization happens on first use; pointer is never NULL after initialization.
Thread-safe via std::call_once.

functions.name: re2::LazyRE2::get
functions.description: Returns the lazily-initialized RE2*, constructing it on first call.
requirements: Safe for concurrent calls; uses std::call_once.
Object is intentionally never deleted.

functions.name: re2::hooks::SetDFAStateCacheResetHook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when a DFA state cache is reset. Pass NULL to clear.
requirements: The callback must be a function with signature void(const DFAStateCacheReset&).
A hook must not assume any lifetime beyond the invocation and must not use RE2 for matching (reentrancy is prohibited).

functions.name: re2::hooks::GetDFAStateCacheResetHook
functions.description: Returns the currently-registered DFA state cache reset hook or NULL if none.
requirements: Returned pointer is just the registered function pointer; no ownership is transferred.

functions.name: re2::hooks::SetDFASearchFailureHook
functions.description: Registers a hook called when DFA search fails. Pass NULL to clear.
requirements: The callback must be a function with signature void(const DFASearchFailure&).
A hook must not assume any lifetime beyond the invocation and must not use RE2 for matching (reentrancy is prohibited).

functions.name: re2::hooks::GetDFASearchFailureHook
functions.description: Returns the currently-registered DFA search failure hook or NULL if none.
requirements: Returned pointer is just the registered function pointer; no ownership is transferred.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Set::Add
functions.signature: int re2::RE2::Set::Add(const re2::StringPiece& pattern, std::string* error)
functions.description: Adds a pattern to the set with the set’s options. Returns the index for the pattern or -1 if parsing fails.
requirements: Must be called before Compile().
error may be NULL; if non-NULL and parsing fails, *error receives the parser’s message.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Set::Compile
functions.description: Compiles the set for matching. Returns false if the compiler runs out of memory. After this, no more Add() calls are allowed.
requirements: Must be called before Match().
Do not call Add() after Compile() returns.

functions.name: re2::RE2::Set::Match
functions.signature: bool re2::RE2::Set::Match(const re2::StringPiece& text, std::vector<int>* v) const
functions.description: Returns true if text matches at least one regexp in the set. If v is non-NULL, fills it with indices of matching regexps (order not guaranteed).
requirements: Compile() must have succeeded before calling Match().
v may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be modified/filled.

data_types.description: A generic, unconstrained sequence of bytes provided by the fuzzer (via FUZZ_PARAM_STR). May contain any characters including NULs. Used as general text, haystack/needle strings, or regex input without requiring any specific encoding or structure.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for interesting arbitrary byte strings tailored for RE2 and StringPiece fuzzers.
# We emphasize valid, diverse inputs: regex patterns (simple/complex), text with varying
# characteristics (ASCII, UTF-8, Latin1, mixed NULs), and rewrite strings with backrefs.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

ASCII = bytes(string.printable, 'ascii')
WHITESPACE = b" \t\r\n\v\f"
PUNCT = b".-_/:,;!?'\"()[]{}<>|@#$%^&*+="
META = b".^$*+?()[]{}|\\"  # regex metacharacters that are significant in RE2
DIGITS = b"0123456789"
HEX = b"0123456789abcdefABCDEF"
OCT = b"01234567"
LETTERS = bytes(string.ascii_letters, 'ascii')

# Some curated regex patterns that are valid in RE2 and exercise various engines paths.
CURATED_PATTERNS = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"a",
    b"abc",
    b".*",
    b"a*",
    b"a+",
    b"a?",
    b"^abc$",
    b"^$",
    b"[a-z]+",
    b"[A-Za-z0-9_]+",
    b"\\d+",
    b"(foo|bar|baz)",
    b"(a)(b)(c)",
    b"(?:ab){1,3}",
    b"a{0,}b?c*",
    b"^foo.*bar$",
    b"[[:alpha:]]+",
    b"(?i)case",
    b"(?-i)CASE",
    b"(?m)^line$",
    b"(?s).+",
    b"\\bword\\b",
    b"\\Bword\\B",
    b"[\xc0-\xff]+",  # Latin1 range
    b"[\x00-\xFF]",
    b"(?'name'[a-z]+)",  # named capture
    b"(?P<n>[0-9]+)",    # alternate named capture syntax accepted by RE2
    b"((?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2}:){5}[0-9a-fA-F]{2})",  # MAC-like
    b"(0[xX][0-9A-Fa-f]+|0[0-7]*|[0-9]+)",       # C-style integer
]

# Text corpus for haystack inputs
TEXT_CORPUS = [
    b"",
    b"a",
    b"hello world",
    b"foo bar baz qux",
    b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
    b"abcxyzABCXYZ0123456789",
    b"line1\nline2\nline3",
    b"tabs\tand\tspaces",
    b"unicode: caf\xc3\xa9 pi\xc3\xb1ata stra\xc3\x9fe",  # UTF-8
    b"latin1: \xe9\xf1\xfc\xe4\xf6",
    b"path/to/file.txt",
    b"email: user@example.com",
    b"url: https://example.org/path?q=1#frag",
    b"aaaaabbbbbaaaaa",
    b"1234567890",
    b"0xDEADBEEF 0755 -42 +17",
]

# Rewrite strings with backreferences \0..\9
REWRITE_TEMPLATES = [
    b"$0",
    b"\\0",
    b"<\\0>",
    b"prefix-\\1-suffix",
    b"A=\\1,B=\\2",
    b"hex=\\1 dec=\\2",
    b"literal_dollar$$ and backref \\0",
]

# Utility creators

def rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def random_utf8(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Build random but valid UTF-8 by sampling code points.
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        t = rng.randrange(5)
        if t == 0:
            # ASCII
            out.append(rng.choice(ASCII))
        elif t == 1:
            # 2-byte
            cp = rng.randrange(0x80, 0x800)
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
        elif t == 2:
            cp = rng.randrange(0x800, 0x10000)
            # Skip surrogates
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                continue
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
        elif t == 3:
            cp = rng.randrange(0x10000, 0x10FFFF)
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            out.append(0)  # occasional NUL
        if len(out) > n:
            break
    return bytes(out[:n])


def make_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(5)
    if choice == 0:
        return rng.choice(CURATED_PATTERNS)
    elif choice == 1:
        # Random literal possibly with meta quoted via QuoteMeta-like escaping
        s = make_text(rng, max_len=64)
        # escape meta with backslashes
        esc = bytearray()
        for b in s:
            if b in META:
                esc.append(ord('\\'))
            esc.append(b)
        return bytes(esc)
    elif choice == 2:
        # Constructed character classes and quantifiers
        parts: List[bytes] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
            k = rng.randrange(4)
            if k == 0:
                parts.append(b"[A-Za-z0-9_]")
            elif k == 1:
                parts.append(b"[0-9]{" + str(rng.randint(1, 5)).encode() + b",}" )
            elif k == 2:
                parts.append(rng.choice([b"\\d+", b"\\w+", b"\\s*", b".+"]))
            else:
                parts.append(b"(" + rng.choice([b"foo", b"bar", b"baz"]) + b"|" + rng.choice([b"qux", b"quux"]) + b")")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.insert(0, b"^")
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(b"$")
        return b"".join(parts)
    elif choice == 3:
        # Inline flags
        flags = []
        if rng.random() < 0.5: flags.append(b"i")
        if rng.random() < 0.3: flags.append(b"m")
        if rng.random() < 0.3: flags.append(b"s")
        core = rng.choice([b"abc", b"[a-z]+", b".*", b"(foo|bar)"])
        return b"(?" + b"".join(flags) + b")" + core
    else:
        # Named groups and backrefs (RE2 supports named but not numeric backrefs in pattern; safe groups only)
        name = rng.choice([b"name", b"grp", b"id"])
        return b"(?P<" + name + b">[0-9]+)" + rng.choice([b"-", b"_", b"" ]) + b"[A-Za-z]*"


def make_text(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    mode = rng.randrange(6)
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    if mode == 0:
        return rng.choice(TEXT_CORPUS)
    elif mode == 1:
        # ASCII with punctuation
        alphabet = ASCII + PUNCT
        return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    elif mode == 2:
        # Valid UTF-8
        return random_utf8(rng, n)
    elif mode == 3:
        # Latin1 bytes
        return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))
    elif mode == 4:
        # Structured numbers and tokens
        tokens = [b"0x", b"-", b"+", b"0", b"x", b"DEAD", b"BEEF", b"0755", b"12345", b"abc", b"XYZ"]
        out = bytearray()
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10)):
            out.extend(rng.choice(tokens))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                out.append(ord(' '))
        return bytes(out[:max_len])
    else:
        # Include NULs and newlines
        base = bytearray()
        for _ in range(n):
            t = rng.randrange(5)
            if t == 0:
                base.append(0)
            elif t == 1:
                base.append(ord('\n'))
            elif t == 2:
                base.append(rng.choice(LETTERS))
            elif t == 3:
                base.append(rng.choice(DIGITS))
            else:
                base.append(rng.choice(PUNCT))
        return bytes(base)


def make_rewrite(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a rewrite mixing literals and backrefs \\0..\\2 to stay within typical veclen used by stubs.
    parts = []
    # Start with a template sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rng.choice(REWRITE_TEMPLATES))
    # Add bounded backrefs
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = rng.randrange(4)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(b" \\0")
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(b" \\1")
        elif choice == 2:
            parts.append(b" \\2")
        else:
            # literal chunk
            chunk = make_text(rng, max_len=16)
            # Avoid accidental escape confusion by escaping backslashes
            chunk = chunk.replace(b"\\", b"\\\\")
            parts.append(chunk)
    return b"".join(parts)[:128]


def assemble_buffers(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    bufs: List[bytes] = []

    # The harness uses many FUZZ_PARAM_STR() occurrences. We'll supply a sequence of
    # interesting buffers in order. A single returned bytes blob will be split by
    # the fuzzer into successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() consumptions.

    # 1) Regex pattern for constructing RE2
    bufs.append(make_pattern(rng))

    # 2) Several general-purpose texts for StringPiece operations and RE2 text
    for _ in range(4):
        bufs.append(make_text(rng, 256))

    # 3) Needles/patterns for starts_with/ends_with/find/rfind/contains
    for _ in range(4):
        bufs.append(make_text(rng, 64))

    # 4) Rewrites for Replace/GlobalReplace/Extract/Rewrite paths
    for _ in range(3):
        bufs.append(make_rewrite(rng))

    # 5) Additional small patterns for RE2::Set
    for _ in range(3):
        bufs.append(make_pattern(rng))

    # 6) More texts to feed after Set compile and matching
    for _ in range(2):
        bufs.append(make_text(rng, 200))

    # 7) Add a few explicitly numeric texts to exercise CRadix/Hex/Octal
    bufs.extend([
        b"0x" + bytes(rng.choice(HEX) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))),
        bytes(rng.choice(OCT) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))),
        b"-" + bytes(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10))),
    ])

    # 8) Include edge cases
    bufs.extend([
        b"",                # empty
        b"\x00",            # single NUL
        b"\n\n\n",        # newlines
        b" ",               # space
        b"\\",              # backslash
        b"[]{}()|^$*+?.",    # many metas
    ])

    # 9) A quoted literal of random text (to validate QuoteMeta expectations)
    literal = make_text(rng, 40)
    # Simple quote by escaping meta characters
    q = bytearray()
    for b in literal:
        if b in META:
            q.append(ord('\\'))
        q.append(b)
    bufs.append(bytes(q))

    # Bound total size and separate buffers with length prefixes so a generic
    # fuzzer harness that reads sequential FUZZ_PARAM_STR() blobs can consume them
    # as independent strings. Here we join with a delimiter unlikely to appear frequently.
    # However, since FUZZ_PARAM_STR takes raw bytes, we simply concatenate with
    # length headers: [u16_len][data] ... so the harness that supports it can split.

    out = bytearray()
    for b in bufs:
        if b is None:
            b = b""
        if len(b) > 1024:
            b = b[:1024]
        # prefix with 2-byte length (little-endian)
        L = len(b)
        out.append(L & 0xFF)
        out.append((L >> 8) & 0xFF)
        out.extend(b)
        if len(out) >= MAX_SIZE:
            break

    return [bytes(out[:MAX_SIZE])]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buffers = assemble_buffers(rng)
    # We produce a single bytes object as required
    return buffers[0]
